title.zh: 卷一百二十四 周書15: 列傳四 王殷 何福進 劉詞 王進 史彥超 史懿 王令溫 周密 李懷忠 白文珂 白延遇 唐景思
title.en: Volume 124 Book of Later Zhou 26: Biographies 4 - Wang Yin, He Fejin, Liu Ci, Wang Jin, Shi Yanchao, Shi Yi, Wang Lingwen, Zhou Mi, Li Huaizong, Bai Wenke, Bai Yanyu, Tang Jinsi
title.raw: 卷一百二十四 周書15: 列傳四 王殷 何福進 劉詞 王進 史彥超 史懿 王令溫 周密 李懷忠 白文珂 白延遇 唐景思 Volume 124 Book of Later Zhou 26: Biographies 4 - Wang Yin, He Fejin, Liu Ci, Wang Jin, Shi Yanchao, Shi Yi, Wang Lingwen, Zhou Mi, Li Huaizong, Bai Wenke, Bai Yanyu, Tang Jinsi

sentences.zh: 王殷，瀛州人。

translations.literal: Wang Yin was a man of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin came from Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖昌裔，本州別駕。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Changyi was acting governor of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Changyi had served as deputy prefect of that commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖光，滄州教練使，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guang was drill commissioner of Cang Prefecture, and the family settled there.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guang was training commissioner at Cangzhou, where the family then made their home.

sentences.zh: 唐末，幽、滄大亂，殷父鹹珪避地南遷，因投於魏軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang, You and Cang were in great disorder; Yin's father Xian Gui fled south to escape the turmoil and joined the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang dynasty collapsed into chaos in Youzhou and Cangzhou, Yin's father Xian Gui fled south and enlisted with the Wei forces.

sentences.zh: 殷自言生於魏州之開元寺，既長從軍，漸為偏將。

translations.literal: Yin said himself that he was born at Kaiyuan Temple in Wei Prefecture; when grown he followed the army and gradually became a junior general.
translations.idiomatic: Yin claimed to have been born at Kaiyuan Temple in Weizhou; once grown he took up arms and rose by degrees to become a field officer.

sentences.zh: 唐同光末，為華州馬步軍副指揮使，因家於華下。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang's Tongguang era he was deputy commander of Hua Prefecture's horse and foot forces, and settled his household below Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In the final year of the Tongguang reign he became deputy commander of the cavalry and infantry at Huazhou and established his family there.

sentences.zh: 天成中，移授靈武都指揮使，久之代還。

translations.literal: In the Tiancheng era he was transferred to be commander of Lingwu, and after a long time was relieved and returned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng period he was appointed commander at Lingwu; after a long tour he was relieved and recalled.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，張令昭據鄴叛，殷從範延光討之，首冒矢石，率先登城，以功授祁州刺史，尋改原州。

translations.literal: In Qingtai, Zhang Lingzhao held Ye in rebellion; Yin followed Fan Yanguang to attack him, first braved arrows and stones, and was first to scale the wall; for merit he was made prefect of Qi Prefecture, soon changed to Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai, when Zhang Lingzhao rebelled and seized Ye, Yin marched with Fan Yanguang to suppress him, took the lead under fire, and was first over the wall. For this he was made prefect of Qizhou, then soon transferred to Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 殷性謙謹好禮，事母以孝聞，每與人結交，過從皆先稟於母，母命不從，殷必不往，雖在軍旅，交遊不雜。

translations.literal: Yin's nature was modest, cautious, and fond of ritual; he was known for filial service to his mother. Whenever he formed friendships, he always reported first to his mother; if his mother did not consent, Yin would certainly not go—even in the army, his associations were not mixed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was modest, courteous, and devoted to propriety, and his filial care for his mother was renowned. Before accepting any social invitation he always asked his mother's leave; if she refused, he would not go. Even amid military life his circle of friends remained narrow and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 及為刺史，政事小有不佳，母察之，立殷於庭，詰責而杖之。

translations.literal: When he became prefect, if government affairs were slightly not good, his mother detected it, made Yin stand in the courtyard, questioned and reproached him, and beat him with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became a prefect, whenever his administration fell even slightly short, his mother would notice, summon him into the courtyard, rebuke him, and have him beaten.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》：殷為刺史，政事有小失，母責之，殷即取杖授婢仆，自笞於母前。）〉

translations.literal: (《Ouyang's History》: When Yin was prefect and there was a small fault in government, his mother reproached him; Yin then took a staff, gave it to maidservants, and flogged himself before his mother.)]
translations.idiomatic: (According to 《Ouyang Xiu's History》: Whenever Yin erred slightly in office, his mother would scold him; he would hand a cane to a servant and have himself beaten in her presence.)]

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，丁內艱，尋有詔起復，授憲州刺史，殷上章辭曰：「臣為末將，出處無損益於國家。

translations.literal: In Jin's Tianfu era he suffered the death of his mother; soon there was an edict to recall him from mourning and appoint him prefect of Xian Prefecture. Yin submitted a memorial declining, saying: 'Your servant is a lowly general; coming forth or staying away brings no benefit or harm to the state.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin Tianfu period he entered mourning for his mother, but the court soon ordered him recalled and named him prefect of Xianzhou. Yin memorialized to decline, writing: 'I am only a minor commander; whether I serve or withdraw makes no difference to the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣本燕人，值鄉國離亂，少罹偏罰，因母鞠養訓導，方得成人，不忍遽釋苴麻，遠離廬墓，伏願許臣終母喪紀。

translations.literal: Your servant is originally a man of Yan; when my native land was torn by disorder I suffered partial punishment in youth, and only through my mother's nurturing and instruction did I become an adult. I cannot bear abruptly to cast off hemp mourning and leave far from the grave mound. I humbly beg permission to complete my mother's mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: I am a native of Yan. In the chaos of our homeland I was once unjustly punished as a youth, and it was only through my mother's care and teaching that I grew to manhood. I cannot bring myself to shed my mourning garb and leave her tomb so soon. I beg Your Majesty to let me observe the full period of filial mourning.

sentences.zh: 」晉高祖嘉而許之。

translations.literal: ' The Jin Gaozu praised this and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: ' Gaozu of Jin commended his plea and granted it.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝嗣位，會殷服闋，召典禁軍，累遷奉國右廂都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Jin's Shaodi succeeded the throne, it happened that Yin's mourning ended; he was summoned to command the palace guard and was repeatedly promoted to commander of the right wing of the Fengguo army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shao of Jin took the throne, Yin had just completed his mourning. He was called to lead the palace guard and rose in time to command the right wing of the Fengguo army.

sentences.zh: 漢祖受命，從討杜重威於鄴下，殷與劉詞皆率先力戰，矢中於首，久之，出折鏃於口中，以是漢祖嘉之。

translations.literal: When Han's founder received the Mandate, he followed to attack Du Chongwei below Ye; Yin and Liu Ci both took the lead and fought fiercely. An arrow struck his head; after a long while he drew out the broken arrowhead from his mouth. For this Han's founder commended him.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Han took power, Yin joined the campaign against Du Chongwei at Ye. He and Liu Ci both led the charge; an arrow struck him in the head, and only after some time did he spit out the broken tip. The Han founder praised him highly for this.

sentences.zh: 乾祐末，遷侍衛步軍都指揮使，領夔州節度使，會契丹寇邊，遣殷領兵屯澶州。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianyou he was moved to commander of the palace guard infantry, and concurrently military governor of Kuizhou. When the Khitans raided the border, Yin was sent to lead troops stationed at Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Qianyou era he became commander of the palace guard infantry and concurrent military governor of Kuizhou. When the Khitans invaded the frontier, he was dispatched to hold Cangzhou with his troops.

sentences.zh: 及李業等作亂，漢隱帝密詔澶帥李洪義遣圖殷，洪義懼不克，反以變告殷，殷與洪義同遣人至鄴，請太祖赴內難。

translations.literal: When Li Ye and others made rebellion, Han's Yindi secretly ordered Cang's commander Li Hongyi to plot against Yin. Hongyi feared he could not succeed and instead reported the plot to Yin. Yin and Hongyi together sent men to Ye to ask the Taizu to come to the inner crisis.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ye and his faction rebelled, the Hidden Emperor of Han secretly ordered Li Hongyi, military governor of Cangzhou, to eliminate Yin. Hongyi, fearing failure, instead warned Yin of the plot. Together they sent envoys to Ye asking Taizu to march against the court conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 殷從平京師，授侍衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Yin followed in pacifying the capital and was appointed commander of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yin followed the campaign that pacified the capital and was made commander of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，授天雄軍節度使，加同平章事，典軍如故。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, he was made military governor of Tianxiong army, added as Tongpingzhangshi, and continued to command the army as before.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu ascended the throne, Yin was appointed military governor of the Tianxiong army and made a co-equal chief councilor while retaining command of the guard.

sentences.zh: 殷赴鎮，以侍衛司局從，凡河北征鎮有戍兵處，鹹稟殷節制。

translations.literal: When Yin went to his post, he took the palace guard staff with him; wherever in Hebei there were garrison troops at military commissions, all were subject to Yin's control.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin departed for his post he took his palace guard staff with him, and every garrisoned command in Hebei fell under his authority.

sentences.zh: 又於民間多方聚斂，太祖聞而惡之，因使宣諭曰：「朕離鄴時，帑廩所儲不少，卿與國家同體，隨要取給，何患無財。

translations.literal: He also on many sides extorted from the people. Taizu heard and detested this, and sent an envoy to proclaim: "When I left Ye, the treasury stores were not few. You and the state share one body—take what you need as required; why worry about lacking funds?"
translations.idiomatic: He also extorted wealth from the populace on many fronts. When Taizu learned of this he was displeased and sent word: "When I left Ye the treasuries were well stocked. You and the state are one; take what you need—why scrape the people for money?"

sentences.zh: 」二年夏，太祖征兗還，殷迎謁於路，宴賜而去。

translations.literal: ' In the second year, summer, Taizu returned from campaigning in Yan; Yin met and paid respects on the road, was feasted and rewarded, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: ' That summer in the second year, as Taizu returned from the Yan campaign, Yin met him on the road, was entertained and rewarded, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及王峻得罪，太祖遣其子飛龍使承誨往鄴，令口諭峻之過惡，以慰其心。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun was punished for offense, Taizu sent his son the Feilong envoy Chenghui to Ye to have him orally relate Jun's faults and crimes, to console his heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun fell from favor, Taizu sent his son Chenghui, the Feilong envoy, to Ye with instructions to recount Jun's offenses aloud and reassure Yin.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，以永壽節上表請覲，太祖雖允其請，且慮殷之不誠，尋遣使止之。

translations.literal: In autumn of the third year, on the Yongshou festival he submitted a memorial requesting an audience. Taizu though he granted the request, also feared Yin's insincerity and soon sent an envoy to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn in the third year he petitioned to attend court on the Yongshou festival. Taizu granted the request in form but doubted his loyalty and soon sent orders forbidding him to come.

sentences.zh: 何福進在鎮州，素惡殷之太橫，福進入朝，摭其陰事以奏之，太祖遂疑之。

translations.literal: He Fujin was at Zhen Prefecture and had long hated Yin's excessive arrogance. Fujin entered court and gathered his secret deeds to memorialize; Taizu then came to doubt him.
translations.idiomatic: He Fujin, stationed at Zhenzhou, had long resented Yin's overbearing conduct. When Fujin came to court he laid out Yin's hidden misdeeds in a memorial, and Taizu began to suspect him.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，以郊禋有日，殷自鎮入覲，太祖令依舊內外巡警。

translations.literal: That winter, as the suburban sacrifice drew near, Yin came from his post to attend court. Taizu ordered him to patrol inside and outside as before.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, with the suburban sacrifice approaching, Yin came from his post to attend court, and Taizu restored him to his former duties of internal and external patrol.

sentences.zh: 殷出入部從不下數百人，又以儀形魁偉，觀者無不聳然。

translations.literal: When Yin went in and out his escort was no fewer than several hundred men, and moreover his bearing was towering; onlookers were all struck with awe.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went abroad he was attended by no fewer than several hundred men, and his towering stature made every onlooker stand in awe.

sentences.zh: 一日，遽入奏曰：「郊禮在近，兵民大集，臣城外防警，請量給甲仗，以備非常。

translations.literal: One day he suddenly entered and memorialized: 'The suburban rites are near; soldiers and civilians are greatly gathered. Your servant guards outside the city—please allot armor and weapons in measure to prepare for the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: One day he rushed in and said: 'The suburban rites are at hand and troops and civilians are massing. I am responsible for security outside the walls. Please issue arms and armor as needed against any emergency.

sentences.zh: 」太祖難之。

translations.literal: ' Taizu found this difficult.
translations.idiomatic: ' Taizu was deeply troubled by the request.

sentences.zh: 時中外以太祖嬰疾，步履稍難，多不視朝，俯逼郊禋，殷有震主之勢，頗憂之。

translations.literal: At the time inside and outside the court, because Taizu was afflicted with illness and his steps were somewhat difficult, he often did not attend court. As the suburban sacrifice pressed near, Yin had the momentum to shake the ruler, and many were quite worried.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the court it was known that Taizu was ill and walked with difficulty, and he seldom held audience. With the sacrifice imminent and Yin displaying the aura of a man who could overshadow his sovereign, anxiety spread on all sides.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃力疾坐於滋德殿，殷入起居，即命執之，尋降制流竄，及出都城，遽殺之，眾情乃安。

translations.literal: Taizu then, forcing himself despite illness, sat in Zide Hall. When Yin entered to inquire after his health, he immediately ordered him seized; soon he issued an edict banishing him in exile, and once outside the capital city he was swiftly killed. Public sentiment then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu dragged himself to Zide Hall. When Yin came to pay his respects, he had him seized at once, issued an edict of exile—and had him killed as soon as he left the capital. Only then did public alarm subside.

sentences.zh: 是歲春末，鄴城寺鐘懸絕而落，又火光出幡竿之上。

translations.literal: That spring's end, at a Ye city temple the bell's suspension broke and it fell; moreover fire-light appeared atop a banner pole.
translations.idiomatic: Late that spring the temple bell at Ye fell when its ropes snapped, and flames were seen dancing atop a banner pole.

sentences.zh: 殷之入覲也，都人餞於離亭，上馬失鐙，翻墮於地，人訝其不祥，果及於禍。

translations.literal: When Yin came to court, the capital people saw him off at the parting pavilion; mounting his horse he lost a stirrup and tumbled to the ground. People marveled at the ill omen, and indeed disaster followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin set out for court the people of the capital saw him off at the farewell pavilion; he lost a stirrup mounting his horse and fell to the ground. Onlookers took it for an evil omen—and calamity soon followed.

sentences.zh: 太祖尋令澶帥鄭仁誨赴鄴，殷次子為衙內指揮使，不出候謁，仁誨誅之，遷其家屬於登州。

translations.literal: Taizu soon ordered Cang's commander Zheng Renhui to go to Ye. Yin's second son was yamen inner commander; he did not come out to meet and pay respects. Renhui executed him and moved the family members to Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu soon sent Zheng Renhui, governor of Cangzhou, to Ye. Yin's second son, a yamen commander, failed to come out to receive him; Renhui had him executed and relocated the family to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 何福進，字善長，太原人。

translations.literal: He Fujin, style name Shanchang, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He Fujin, whose style was Shanchang, came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父神劍，累贈左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Shenjian was posthumously promoted repeatedly to Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shenjian was posthumously honored as Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 福進少從軍，以驍勇聞。

translations.literal: Fujin in youth followed the army and was known for fierce courage.
translations.idiomatic: Fujin took up arms young and won renown for bold fighting.

sentences.zh: 唐同光末，郭從謙以兵圍莊宗於大內，福進時為宿衛軍校，獨出死力拒戰於內，後明宗知而嘉之，擢為捧聖軍校，出為磁州刺史，充北面行營先鋒都校。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang Tongguang, Guo Congqian with troops besieged Zhuangzong in the inner palace. Fujin at the time was a night-guard army officer and alone exerted deadly force resisting inside. Later Mingzong learned and praised this, promoted him to Fengsheng army officer, sent him out as prefect of Ci Prefecture, and made him vanguard commander of the northern campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Tongguang era Guo Congqian besieged Zhuangzong in the inner palace. Fujin, then a night-guard officer, fought alone with desperate valor inside the walls. Mingzong learned of this and commended him, promoting him in the Fengsheng guard, appointing him prefect of Cizhou, and naming him vanguard commander of the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，自彰聖都虞候率本軍從範延光平鄴，以功歷鄭、隴二州防禦使。

translations.literal: In Qingtai, from Zhangsheng deputy commander he led his army following Fan Yanguang to pacify Ye; for merit he successively served as defense commissioner of Zheng and Long prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: During Qingtai he led his Zhangsheng troops with Fan Yanguang to pacify Ye and, for his service, served in turn as defense commissioner of Zhengzhou and Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 開運中，由潁州團練使入拜左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In Kaiyun he entered court from Yingzhou regiment trainer to pay homage as Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaiyun he came to court from his post as regiment trainer of Yingzhou and was appointed Grand General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 屬契丹陷中原，令中朝文武臣僚凡數十人隨帳北歸，時福進預其行。

translations.literal: When the Khitans overran the Central Plains, they ordered several tens of civil and military officials of the central court to follow the camp north in return. At the time Fujin was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans overran the Central Plains they compelled several dozen court officials to march north with their camp, and Fujin was among them.

sentences.zh: 行次鎮州，聞北主已斃，其黨尚據鎮陽，遂與李筠、白再榮之儔合謀力戰，盡逐契丹，據有鎮陽。

translations.literal: Stopping at Zhen Prefecture, they heard the northern ruler had died but his faction still held Zhenyang. Thereupon with Li Jun, Bai Zairong, and their kind they joined in plotting and fought fiercely, completely driving out the Khitans and seizing Zhenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Halting at Zhenzhou they learned the Khitan emperor was dead though his followers still held Zhenyang. Fujin joined Li Jun, Bai Zairong, and others in a fierce rising that drove the Khitans out and took the city.

sentences.zh: 時漢祖已建號於河東，詔以福進為北面行營馬步都虞候，尋拜曹州防禦使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: At the time Han's founder had already established his title in Hedong; he was ordered as northern campaign horse and foot deputy commander, soon appointed Cao Prefecture defense commissioner and acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Han founder had proclaimed his reign in Hedong. Fujin was named deputy commander of the northern campaign's cavalry and infantry, then made defense commissioner of Caozhou and Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 太祖出鎮於鄴，將謀北伐，奏以福進自隨。

translations.literal: When Taizu went out to garrison Ye, planning a northern campaign, he memorialized to have Fujin follow him personally.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took up his post at Ye and prepared a northern campaign, he asked that Fujin accompany him.

sentences.zh: 及太祖入平內難，以輔佐功拜忠武軍節度使，不數月，移領鎮州。

translations.literal: When Taizu entered to pacify the inner crisis, for assisting merit he was made military governor of Zhongwu army; within a few months he was transferred to lead Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu quelled the court crisis, Fujin was made military governor of the Zhongwu army; within months he was transferred to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 數年之間，北鄙無事。

translations.literal: Within several years the northern marches were without incident.
translations.idiomatic: For several years the northern frontier remained quiet under his rule.

sentences.zh: 及聞太祖將有事於南郊，拜章入覲，改天平軍節度使，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When he heard Taizu would conduct affairs at the southern suburb, he submitted a memorial to attend court, was changed to military governor of Tianping army, and added as Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Taizu would perform the suburban sacrifice, he petitioned for an audience, was transferred to the Tianping army, and made a co-equal chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 未及之任，卒於東京之私第，年六十有六，時顯德元年正月也。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post he died at his private residence in the Eastern Capital, age sixty-six; it was the first month of Xiande's first year.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the new post he died at his home in the Eastern Capital, aged sixty-six, in the first month of the first year of Xiande.

sentences.zh: 累贈中書令。

translations.literal: He was posthumously promoted repeatedly to Zhongshuling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子繼筠，仕皇朝，領建武軍節度使卒。

translations.literal: His son Jijun served the imperial court, held the post of military governor of Jianwu army, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jijun served the dynasty as military governor of the Jianwu army and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 劉詞，字好謙，元城人。

translations.literal: Liu Ci, style name Haoqian, was a man of Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ci, whose style was Haoqian, came from Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，事故鄴帥楊師厚，以勇悍聞。

translations.literal: In Liang's Zhenming era he served under former Ye commander Yang Shihou and was known for fierce valor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liang Zhenming era he served under Yang Shihou, the former governor of Ye, and won fame for fierce fighting.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗入魏，亦列於麾下，兩河之戰，無不預焉。

translations.literal: When Tang's Zhuangzong entered Wei he was also ranked under his banner; of the battles between the two rivers, none did he not take part in.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong of Tang entered Wei, Ci joined his ranks and took part in nearly every battle fought between the Yellow and Bian rivers.

sentences.zh: 同光初，為效節軍使，轉劍直指揮使，尋以忤於權臣，出為汝州小校，凡留滯十餘年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was Xiaojie army commander, transferred to Jianzhi commander; soon for offending a powerful minister he was sent out as a minor officer of Ruzhou, and in all was detained over ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongguang he commanded the Xiaojie army, then the Jianzhi guard, but after offending a powerful minister was demoted to a junior post at Ruzhou and languished there for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，詔諸道選驍果以實禁衛，由是得入典禁軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai an edict ordered each circuit to select fierce warriors to fill the palace guard; thereby he was able to enter and command the palace army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai the throne ordered each circuit to send its bravest men to fill the palace guard, and through this Ci reentered imperial service.

sentences.zh: 晉初，從侯益收汜水關，佐楊光遠平鄴都，累遷奉國第一軍都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin he followed Hou Yi to recover the Sishui Pass, assisted Yang Guangyuan to pacify the Ye capital, and was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the first Fengguo army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jin he followed Hou Yi to recover Sishui Pass, aided Yang Guangyuan in pacifying Ye, and rose to deputy commander of the first Fengguo army.

sentences.zh: 後從馬全節伐安陸，敗淮賊萬餘眾，晉祖嘉之，授奉國都校，累加檢校司空。

translations.literal: Later he followed Ma Quanjie to attack Anlu, defeated more than ten thousand Huai bandits; Jin's ancestor praised this, appointed him Fengguo army commander, and repeatedly added Acting Sikong.
translations.idiomatic: He later joined Ma Quanjie against Anlu and routed more than ten thousand Huai rebels. The Jin emperor commended him, made him commander of the Fengguo army, and promoted him to Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 又從杜重威敗安重榮於宗城。

translations.literal: He also followed Du Chongwei to defeat An Chongrong at Zongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Du Chongwei in the defeat of An Chongrong at Zongcheng.

sentences.zh: 及圍鎮陽，詞自登雲梯，身先士伍，以功加檢校司徒、沁州刺史。

translations.literal: When besieging Zhenyang, Ci himself climbed the cloud ladder, took the lead before the soldiers, and for merit was added Acting Situ and made prefect of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Zhenyang he climbed the assault ladder himself and led the charge, earning promotion to Acting Minister of Education and appointment as prefect of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 時王師方討襄陽，尋命詞兼行營都虞候，襄陽平，遷本州團練使。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial army was just attacking Xiangyang; soon Ci was ordered concurrently as campaign deputy commander. When Xiangyang was pacified he was moved to regiment trainer of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: While the imperial army was campaigning against Xiangyang, Ci was named deputy commander of the expedition; when the city fell he became regiment trainer of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 在郡歲餘，臨事之暇，必被甲枕戈而臥，人或問之，詞曰：「我以勇敢而登貴仕，不可一日而忘本也。

translations.literal: In the prefecture over a year, in leisure from governing affairs he would always don armor and sleep with weapon as pillow. When people asked, Ci said: 'I rose to noble office through courage—I cannot for one day forget my origin.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year in office, whenever he had a spare moment he would sleep in armor with his weapon for a pillow. When asked why, Ci said: 'I won high rank through courage; I must not forget that for a single day.

sentences.zh: 若信其溫飽，則筋力有怠，將來何以報國也！

translations.literal: If I trust in warmth and full belly, then sinew and strength will slacken—how in the future can I repay the state!
translations.idiomatic: If I grow soft with comfort, my strength will fail—how then could I repay the state in the days ahead!

sentences.zh: 」及漢有天下，復為奉國右廂都校，遙領閬州防禦使。

translations.literal: ' When Han possessed the realm, he again became commander of the Fengguo right wing and remotely held Lang Prefecture defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: ' When Han ruled the realm he again commanded the right wing of the Fengguo army and held the defense commission of Langzhou in absentia.

sentences.zh: 從太祖平鄴，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: Following Taizu in pacifying Ye, he was added Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizu in pacifying Ye and was promoted to Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 乾祐初，李守貞叛於河中，太祖征之，朝廷以為侍衛步軍都指揮使，遙領寧江軍節度使，充行營馬步都虞候，命分屯於河西。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou, Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong; Taizu campaigned against him. The court made Ci commander of palace guard infantry, remotely military governor of Ningjiang army, and campaign horse and foot deputy commander, ordering him to divide encampments west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianyou, when Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong, Taizu marched against him. The court named Ci commander of the palace guard infantry, concurrent military governor of the Ningjiang army, and deputy commander of the expedition, with orders to encamp west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，守貞遣敢死之士數千，夜入其營。

translations.literal: In the second year, first month, Shouzhen sent several thousand death-defying warriors who at night entered his camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Shouzhen sent several thousand suicide troops in a night assault on his camp.

sentences.zh: 皆怖懼不知所為，惟詞神氣自若，令於軍中曰：「此小盜耳，不足驚也。

translations.literal: All were terrified and did not know what to do; only Ci's spirit and bearing were as usual. He ordered in the army: 'These are small bandits—not worth alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The camp panicked, but Ci alone remained composed. He called out to the troops: 'These are mere raiders—nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 」遂免胄橫戈，叱短兵以擊之，賊眾大敗而退。

translations.literal: ' Thereupon he removed his helmet, held his halberd crosswise, shouted at short weapons to strike them, and the rebel host was greatly defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: ' He doffed his helmet, seized his halberd, and drove the skirmishers forward; the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 自是守貞喪膽，不復有奔突之意。

translations.literal: From this Shouzhen lost his gall and no longer had the will for sudden raids.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Shouzhen lost heart and attempted no further sorties.

sentences.zh: 河中平，太祖嘉之，表其功為華州節度使，歲餘，移鎮邢臺。

translations.literal: When Hezhong was pacified, Taizu praised him and memorialized his merit as military governor of Hua Prefecture; after a year and more he was moved to garrison Xingtai.
translations.idiomatic: When Hezhong fell, Taizu commended him and had him made military governor of Huazhou; a year later he was transferred to Xingtai.

sentences.zh: 太祖受命，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the Mandate, he was added Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Ci was made a co-equal chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，改鎮河陽。

translations.literal: In autumn of the third year he was changed to garrison Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn in the third year he was transferred to Heyang.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，世宗親征劉崇，詞奉命領所部兵隨駕，行及高平南，遇樊愛能等自北退回，且言官軍已敗，止詞不行，詞不聽，疾驅而北。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, Shizong personally campaigned against Liu Chong; Ci received orders to lead his troops following the imperial carriage. Marching to south of Gaoping, he met Fan Aineng and others returning from the north, who also said the imperial army had been defeated and urged Ci not to advance. Ci would not listen and spurred swiftly north.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande, when Shizong marched in person against Liu Chong, Ci led his troops with the imperial train. South of Gaoping he met Fan Aineng and others fleeing south, who claimed the army had been routed and begged him to turn back. Ci refused and pressed north at full speed.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞而嘉之，尋命為隨駕都部署，又授河東道行營副部署。

translations.literal: Shizong heard and praised this; soon he was ordered as attendant-campaign chief deployer, and also given deputy deployer of the Hedong circuit campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong heard of this and commended him, soon naming him chief deployer of the imperial train and deputy deployer of the Hedong expedition.

sentences.zh: 其年夏，車駕還京，授永興軍節度使，加兼侍中，行京兆尹。

translations.literal: That summer the imperial carriage returned to the capital; he was made military governor of Yongxing army, added concurrently as Palace Attendant, and acted as Jingzhao governor.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when the emperor returned to the capital, Ci was made military governor of the Yongxing army, appointed Palace Attendant, and entrusted with the duties of Jingzhao governor.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，以疾卒於鎮，年六十有五。

translations.literal: In winter of the second year he died of illness at his post, age sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at his post that winter in the second year, aged sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令，謚曰忠惠。

translations.literal: He was gifted Zhongshuling; posthumous title Loyal and Kind.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous name Loyal and Kind.

sentences.zh: 詞發身軍校，亟歷戎事，常以忠勇自負。

translations.literal: Ci rose from army officer, quickly passed through military affairs, and always prided himself on loyalty and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Ci had risen from the ranks, seen constant warfare, and prided himself on loyalty and valor.

sentences.zh: 洎領藩鎮，能靖恭為治，無苛政以撓民，謚以忠惠，議者韙之。

translations.literal: When he came to lead a military commission, he could govern with calm respect, had no harsh government to disturb the people; the posthumous title Loyal and Kind—commentators approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held a frontier command he governed with quiet dignity and imposed no harsh levies on the people; commentators agreed that the posthumous name Loyal and Kind was well deserved.

sentences.zh: 子延欽，仕皇朝為控鶴廂使。

translations.literal: His son Yanqin served the imperial court as commander of the Konghe wing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanqin served the dynasty as commander of the Konghe guard wing.

sentences.zh: 史彥超，雲州人也。

translations.literal: Shi Yanchao was a man of Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yanchao came from Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 性驍獷，有膽氣，累功至龍捷都指揮使。

translations.literal: His nature was fierce and overbearing; he had daring spirit and through accumulated merit reached commander of the Longjie army.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce and domineering by nature, bold in spirit, he rose through repeated merit to command the Longjie army.

sentences.zh: 太祖之赴內難，彥超以本軍從。

translations.literal: When Taizu went to the inner crisis, Yanchao followed with his army.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched to quell the court crisis, Yanchao followed with his troops.

sentences.zh: 國初，與虎捷都指揮使何徵戍晉州，會劉崇與契丹入寇，攻圍州城月餘，是時本州無帥，知州王萬敢不協物情，彥超與何徵協力固拒，累挫敵鋒。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state, with Hujie commander He Zheng he garrisoned Jin Prefecture. When Liu Chong and the Khitans invaded, they attacked and besieged the prefectural city for more than a month. At the time the prefecture had no commander; prefect Wang Wan was bold but did not harmonize with public sentiment. Yanchao and He Zheng cooperated in firm resistance and repeatedly blunted the enemy's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the dynasty he and He Zheng of the Hujie guard garrisoned Jinzhou. When Liu Chong and the Khitans invaded they besieged the city for more than a month. The circuit had no military governor, and the prefect Wang Wan, though brave, had alienated local opinion. Yanchao and He Zheng held the city together and repeatedly repulsed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 攻擊日急，禦捍有備，軍政甚嚴，居人無擾。

translations.literal: As attacks grew daily more urgent, defense was prepared; military government was very strict, and residents were undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: As the assaults intensified daily, their defenses held firm, military discipline remained strict, and the civilian population was left unmolested.

sentences.zh: 及朝廷遣樞密使王峻總兵為援，敵兵宵遁。

translations.literal: When the court sent Privy Councilor Wang Jun to command troops as relief, the enemy army fled in the night.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sent Privy Councilor Wang Jun with a relief army, the enemy withdrew under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其善守之功，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: Taizu praised their merit in good defense and rewarded them very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu commended their stout defense and rewarded them handsomely.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授龍捷右廂都指揮使，尋授鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: Before long he was made commander of the Longjie right wing; soon he was appointed Zheng Prefecture defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named commander of the right wing of the Longjie army, then defense commissioner of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 劉崇之寇潞州也，車駕親征，以彥超為先鋒都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Liu Chong raided Lu Prefecture, the imperial carriage campaigned in person and made Yanchao vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong attacked Luzhou the emperor marched in person and appointed Yanchao vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 高平之戰，先登陷陣，以功授華州節度使，先鋒如故。

translations.literal: At the battle of Gaoping he was first to ascend and break the formation; for merit he was made military governor of Hua Prefecture while remaining vanguard as before.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaoping he was first over the wall and into the enemy line; for this he was made military governor of Huazhou while retaining command of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 大軍至河東城下，契丹營於忻、代之間，遙應賊勢，詔天雄軍節度使符彥卿率諸將屯忻州以拒之。

translations.literal: The great army reached below the Hedong city wall; the Khitans encamped between Xin and Dai, responding from afar to the rebel momentum. An edict ordered Tianxiong military governor Fu Yanqing to lead the generals to encamp at Xin Prefecture to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army reached the walls of Hedong, the Khitans camped between Xinzhou and Daizhou in support of the enemy. The throne ordered Fu Yanqing, military governor of the Tianxiong army, to lead the generals to Xinzhou to block them.

sentences.zh: 彥卿襲契丹於忻口。

translations.literal: Yanqing raided the Khitans at Xinkou.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing attacked the Khitans at Xinkou.

sentences.zh: 彥超以先鋒軍追蕃寇，離大軍稍遠，賊兵伏發，為賊所陷。

translations.literal: Yanchao with the vanguard army pursued the barbarian bandits, straying somewhat far from the great army; rebel troops sprang from ambush and he was trapped by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao pursued the enemy with the vanguard, outrunning the main force, and fell into an ambush.

sentences.zh: 世宗痛惜久之，詔贈太師，示加等也，仍命優恤其家焉。

translations.literal: Shizong grieved long; an edict posthumously gifted Grand Preceptor, showing elevated rank, and still ordered generous relief for his family.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong mourned him deeply, posthumously honoring him as Grand Preceptor—the highest rank—and ordering special care for his family.

sentences.zh: 史懿，字繼美，代郡人也。

translations.literal: Shi Yi, style name Jimei, was a man of Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yi, whose style was Jimei, came from Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 本名犯太祖廟諱，故改焉。

translations.literal: His original name violated Taizu's temple taboo, so it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name violated the taboo of Taizu's temple name, and so it was changed.

sentences.zh: 父建瑭，事唐莊宗為先鋒都校，《唐書》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Jiantang served Tang's Zhuangzong as vanguard commander; the 《Tang History》 has his biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiantang had served Zhuangzong of Tang as a vanguard commander and has a biography in the 《Tang History》.

sentences.zh: 莊宗之伐鎮陽，時建瑭為流矢所中而卒，懿時年甫弱冠，莊宗以其父歿於王事，召拜昭德軍使，俄遷先鋒左右廂都校，俾嗣其家聲。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong attacked Zhenyang, at the time Jiantang was struck by a stray arrow and died. Yi was then just past weak crown; Zhuangzong because his father died in royal service summoned and appointed him Zhaode army commander, soon moved to vanguard left and right wing commander, enabling him to inherit the family's renown.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong campaigned against Zhenyang, Jiantang was killed by a stray arrow. Yi was then barely twenty. Zhuangzong, honoring his father's death in the ruler's service, appointed Yi commander of the Zhaode army and soon made him commander of both vanguard wings, that he might carry on the family name.

sentences.zh: 天成中，為涿州刺史。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng he was made prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiancheng era he was appointed prefect of Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 晉初，由趙州刺史遷洺州團練使，尋歷亳、鳳二州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, from Zhao Prefecture prefect he was moved to Mingzhou regiment trainer, soon successively served as defense commissioner of Bo and Feng prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jin he moved from the prefecture of Zhao to regiment trainer of Mingzhou, then served in turn as defense commissioner of Bozhou and Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉祖以其弟翰尚晉國長公主，故尤所註意。

translations.literal: Jin's ancestor because his younger brother Han married the Jin state's eldest imperial princess therefore paid him especial attention.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yi's younger brother Han had married the Jin state's eldest imperial princess, the Jin emperor took special notice of him.

sentences.zh: 天福中，授彰武軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: In Tianfu he was appointed Zhangwu army military governor and observation acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu he was made acting military governor and observation commissioner of the Zhangwu army.

sentences.zh: 開運初，歷澶、貝二鎮節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he successively served as military governor of the Cang and Bei commands.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyun he served in turn as military governor of Cangzhou and Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，移鎮涇原。

translations.literal: In the third year he was moved to garrison Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，契丹入中原，時四方征鎮為契丹所召者靡不灊至，惟懿堅壁拒命，仍送款於漢祖。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitans entered the Central Plains. At the time of the four directions' military commissions summoned by the Khitans, none failed to arrive in haste—only Yi held firm behind walls and refused orders, yet still sent allegiance to Han's founder.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Khitans overran the Central Plains. Every frontier command summoned by them hurried to obey—only Yi barred his gates and refused, while sending his allegiance to the Han founder.

sentences.zh: 漢有天下，就拜檢校太尉、同平章事，及賜功臣名號。

translations.literal: When Han possessed the realm, he was at once appointed Acting Grand Commandant and Tongpingzhangshi, and was also granted a meritorious subject title.
translations.idiomatic: When Han ruled the realm he was confirmed as Acting Grand Commandant and co-equal chief councilor, and granted a meritorious subject title.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，加檢校太師、兼侍中，進封邠國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was added Acting Grand Preceptor and concurrent Palace Attendant, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangshun he was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor and Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Bin.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年春，以抱病歸朝。

translations.literal: In spring of Xiande's first year, because he embraced illness he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Xiande he returned to court, ill in body.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·楊廷璋傳》：周太祖常諭廷璋圖涇帥史懿，廷璋屏左右，示以詔書，懿受代入朝，遂免禍。）〉

translations.literal: (《Eastern Capital Affairs Outline - Biography of Yang Tingzhang》: Zhou's Taizu often instructed Tingzhang to plot against Jing commander Shi Yi. Tingzhang dismissed those at his side and showed him the edict; Yi accepted replacement and entered court, and thereby escaped calamity.)]
translations.idiomatic: (According to the Eastern Capital Affairs Outline, biography of Yang Tingzhang: Taizu of Zhou often directed Tingzhang to remove the Jing commander Shi Yi. Tingzhang dismissed his attendants and showed Yi the edict; Yi accepted recall and came to court, thus escaping disaster.)]

sentences.zh: 途經洛，卒於其第，年六十三。

translations.literal: Passing through Luo, he died at his residence, age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: En route through Luoyang he died at his residence, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令。

translations.literal: He was posthumously gifted Zhongshuling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 王令溫，字順之，瀛州河間人也。

translations.literal: Wang Lingwen, style name Shunzhi, was a man of Hejian in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lingwen, whose style was Shunzhi, came from Hejian in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父迪，德州刺史，累贈太子太師。

translations.literal: His father Di was De Prefecture prefect and was repeatedly posthumously promoted to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Di had been prefect of Dezhou and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 令溫少以武勇稱，初隸唐莊宗麾下，稍遷廳直軍校。

translations.literal: Lingwen in youth was known for martial valor; he first served under Tang's Zhuangzong and was gradually promoted to hall-direct army officer.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwen won early fame for martial valor, first entering service under Zhuangzong of Tang and rising to become an officer of the hall-direct guard.

sentences.zh: 明宗之為統帥，嘗與契丹戰於上谷，明宗臨陣馬逸，為敵所迫，令溫乃以所乘馬授明宗，而自力戰，飛矢連發，敵兵為之稍卻。

translations.literal: When Mingzong was commander-in-chief, he once battled the Khitans at Shanggu. Mingzong at the front had his horse bolt and was pressed by the enemy. Lingwen then gave Mingzong the horse he rode and himself fought with full strength, arrows flying in succession, and the enemy troops for this retreated somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong was supreme commander he once fought the Khitans at Shanggu. Mingzong's mount bolted under fire and the enemy closed in; Lingwen gave him his own horse and fought on foot, loosing arrow after arrow until the enemy drew back.

sentences.zh: 及明宗即位，歷遷神武彰聖都校。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to Shenwu-Zhangsheng army commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingzong ascended the throne, Lingwen rose to command the Shenwu-Zhangsheng army.

sentences.zh: 晉初，自淄州刺史遷洺州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin, from Zi Prefecture prefect he was moved to Mingzhou regiment trainer.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jin he moved from prefect of Zizhou to regiment trainer of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及安重榮稱兵於鎮州，晉祖以令溫為行營馬軍都指揮使，與都帥杜重威敗賊於宗城，以功授亳州防禦使，尋拜永清軍節度使。

translations.literal: When An Chongrong raised troops at Zhen Prefecture, Jin's ancestor made Lingwen campaign cavalry commander; with supreme commander Du Chongwei he defeated the rebels at Zongcheng. For merit he was made Bozhou defense commissioner, soon appointed Yongqing army military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When An Chongrong rebelled at Zhenzhou, the Jin emperor named Lingwen commander of the expedition's cavalry. With Du Chongwei he routed the rebels at Zongcheng, was made defense commissioner of Bozhou, and soon military governor of the Yongqing army.

sentences.zh: 屬契丹來寇，時令溫奉詔入朝，契丹遂陷貝州，其家屬因沒於契丹。

translations.literal: When the Khitans came to raid, at the time Lingwen received orders to enter court; the Khitans then captured Bei Prefecture, and his family members thereby were lost to the Khitans.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans invaded, Lingwen was summoned to court; they then seized Beizhou, and his family fell into Khitan hands.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝憫之，授武勝軍節度使。

translations.literal: Jin's Shaodi pitied him and appointed him military governor of the Wusheng army.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shao of Jin took pity on him and made him military governor of the Wusheng army.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移鎮延州，又遷靈武。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to garrison Yan Prefecture, then transferred to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Yanzhou, then to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 漢有天下，復為永清軍節度使，尋改安州。

translations.literal: When Han possessed the realm, he again became Yongqing army military governor; soon he was changed to An Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Han ruled the realm he again governed the Yongqing army, then was transferred to Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 國初，加檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was added Acting Grand Commandant and Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he was made Acting Grand Commandant and co-equal chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣位，遷鎮安軍節度使，罷鎮歸闕。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded the throne, he was moved to Zhen'an army military governor, then ceased his post and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded the throne, Lingwen was transferred to the Zhen'an army, then relinquished his command and returned to court.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年夏，以疾卒，時年六十有二，詔贈侍中。

translations.literal: In summer of Xiande's third year he died of illness, then age sixty-two; an edict posthumously gifted Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness that summer in the third year of Xiande, aged sixty-two; the throne posthumously honored him as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 長子銳，仕皇朝為內職。

translations.literal: His eldest son Rui served the imperial court in inner service.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Rui served the dynasty in a palace post.

sentences.zh: 次子廣，歷諸衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His second son Guang successively served as grand general of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Guang rose to grand general in the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 李懷忠，字光孝，太原晉陽人。

translations.literal: Li Huaizhong, style name Guangxiao, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaizhong, whose style was Guangxiao, came from Jinyang in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父海，本府軍校。

translations.literal: His father Hai was an army officer of the native prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hai had been an army officer of the prefectural command.

sentences.zh: 懷忠形質魁壯，初事唐莊宗，隸於保衛軍。

translations.literal: Huaizhong's form and substance were towering and strong; he first served Tang's Zhuangzong and was attached to the Guard army.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhong was tall and powerfully built; he first served Zhuangzong of Tang in the Guard army.

sentences.zh: 夾城之役，懷忠率先登城，以功補本軍副兵馬使。

translations.literal: At the battle of Jiacheng, Huaizhong was first to scale the wall; for merit he was supplemented as deputy horse-and-troop commander of his army.
translations.idiomatic: At the siege of Jiacheng he was first over the wall and was promoted to deputy commander of his army's cavalry.

sentences.zh: 莊宗平定山東，累遷保衛軍使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Shandong, he was repeatedly promoted to Guard army commander.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong pacified Shandong, Huaizhong rose to command the Guard army.

sentences.zh: 天成中，歷陜府、許州、滄州都指揮使，遙領辰州刺史。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng he successively served as commander of Shaanfu, Xuzhou, and Cangzhou, and remotely held Chen Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng he commanded the forces at Shaanfu, Xuzhou, and Cangzhou in turn, and held the prefecture of Chenzhou in absentia.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，以河西蕃部寇鈔，命懷忠屯方渠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, because Hexi tribal departments raided and plundered, Huaizhong was ordered to encamp at Fangqu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai, when Hexi tribes raided the frontier, Huaizhong was ordered to encamp at Fangqu.

sentences.zh: 晉祖受命，以懷忠故人，召典禁兵，三遷護聖左右廂都指揮使，遙領壽州節度使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: When Jin's ancestor received the Mandate, because Huaizhong was an old acquaintance he was summoned to command the palace guard, thrice promoted to commander of the Husheng left and right wings, remotely military governor of Shou Prefecture and Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder took power he recalled his old comrade Huaizhong to lead the palace guard, promoted him three times to commander of both Husheng wings, and named him concurrent military governor of Shouzhou and Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為同州節度使、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: Before long he became Tong Prefecture military governor and Acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made military governor of Tongzhou and Acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 少帝嗣位，入為右羽林統軍，改左武衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When Shaodi succeeded the throne, he entered as commander of the Right Yulin Guard, changed to Left Wuwei Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao succeeded the throne, Huaizhong entered court as commander of the Right Yulin Guard, then became Grand General of the Left Wuwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 廣順中，以太子太傅致仕。

translations.literal: In Guangshun he retired with the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangshun he retired with the rank of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 三年夏卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year he died, age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died that summer in the third year, aged sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太子太師。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously gifted Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously honored him as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 白文珂，字德溫，太原人也。

translations.literal: Bai Wenke, style name Dewen, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Wenke, whose style was Dewen, came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖辯。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Bian.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather was named Bian.

sentences.zh: 父君成，遼州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Juncheng was Lia Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His father Juncheng had been prefect of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 文珂初事後唐武皇，補河東牙將，改遼州副使。

translations.literal: Wenke first served Later Tang's Martial Emperor, was supplemented as a Hedong guards officer, and changed to Lia Prefecture deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wenke first served the Martial Emperor of Later Tang as a Hedong guards officer, then became deputy commissioner of Liaozhou.

sentences.zh: 莊宗嗣位，轉振武都指揮使。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong succeeded the throne, he was transferred to Zhenwu army commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong succeeded the throne, Wenke was made commander of the Zhenwu army.

sentences.zh: 天成中，鎮州節度使王建立表為本州馬步軍都指揮使，遙授舒州刺史、檢校司空，歷青州、魏府都指揮使，歷瀛、蔚、忻、代四州刺史。

translations.literal: In Tiancheng, Zhen Prefecture military governor Wang Jianli memorialized him as that prefecture's horse and foot commander, remotely appointed Shu Prefecture prefect and Acting Sikong, successively served as Qingzhou and Weifu commander, and successively served as prefect of Ying, Yu, Xin, and Dai—the four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiancheng, Wang Jianli, military governor of Zhenzhou, recommended him as commander of its cavalry and infantry; he was named prefect of Shuzhou in absentia and Acting Minister of Works, later commanded at Qingzhou and Weifu, and served in turn as prefect of Yingzhou, Yuzhou, Xinzhou, and Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 領代州日，兼蕃漢馬步都部署。

translations.literal: On the days he held Daizhou, he concurrently was overall deployer of barbarian and Han horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: While governing Daizhou he also served as overall deployer of tribal and Han cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖鎮並門，表為副留守、檢校太保。

translations.literal: When Han's Gaozu garrisoned Bingmen, he was memorialized as deputy defender and Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu of Han held Bingmen he was named deputy defender and Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 漢國初建，授河中節度使、西南面招討使、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When Han's state was first established, he was appointed Hezhong military governor, southwest pacification commissioner, and Acting Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Han he was made military governor of Hezhong, commissioner for pacifying the southwest, and Acting Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 漢祖定兩京，改天平軍節度使，加同平章事。

translations.literal: When Han's founder settled the two capitals, he was changed to Tianping army military governor and added Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: After the Han founder secured the two capitals, Wenke was transferred to the Tianping army and made a co-equal chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鎮陜州，檢校太師。

translations.literal: Before long he garrisoned Shan Prefecture as Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Shanzhou as Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 會河中李守貞叛，詔充河中府行營都部署。

translations.literal: When Hezhong's Li Shouzhen rebelled, an edict appointed him overall deployer of the Hezhong prefecture campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong, an edict named him overall deployer of the Hezhong expedition.

sentences.zh: 時文珂已老，朝議恐非守貞之敵，乃命太祖西征。

translations.literal: At the time Wenke was already old; court discussion feared he was not Shouzhen's match, and therefore ordered Taizu to campaign west.
translations.idiomatic: Wenke was by then elderly, and the court feared he could not overcome Shouzhen, so Taizu was ordered to take command in the west.

sentences.zh: 河中平，文珂授西京留守、河南尹。

translations.literal: When Hezhong was pacified, Wenke was appointed western capital defender and Henan governor.
translations.idiomatic: After Hezhong fell, Wenke was made defender of the western capital and governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 太祖踐阼，加兼中書令，頃之，以太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: When Taizu ascended the throne, he was added concurrently as Zhongshuling; shortly thereafter he retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Wenke was also named Director of the Secretariat; soon afterward he retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，封晉國公。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin.

sentences.zh: 顯德元年，卒於西京，年七十九。

translations.literal: In Xiande's first year he died in the western capital, age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the western capital in the first year of Xiande, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 輟視朝一日。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: The court suspended audiences for one day in mourning.

sentences.zh: 子廷誨，仕皇朝，歷諸衛將軍卒。

translations.literal: His son Tinghui served the imperial court, successively served as guard general, and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tinghui served the dynasty as a guard general and died in office.

sentences.zh: 白延遇，字希望，太原人也。

translations.literal: Bai Yanyu, style name Xiwang, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Yanyu, whose style was Xiwang, came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 幼畜於晉之公宮，年十三，從晉祖伐蜀，以趫悍見稱。

translations.literal: In youth he was raised in Jin's public palace; at age thirteen he followed Jin's ancestor to campaign against Shu and was acclaimed for leaping fierceness.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised from childhood in the Jin princely household; at thirteen he joined the Jin founder's campaign against Shu and won fame for his fierce agility.

sentences.zh: 晉有天下，歷典禁軍，累遷至檢校司空。

translations.literal: When Jin possessed the realm, he successively commanded the palace guard and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Sikong.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin ruled the realm he held successive commands in the palace guard and rose to Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 天福中，晉祖在鄴，安重榮叛於鎮州，帥眾數萬詣闕而來，晉祖命杜重威統諸將以禦之。

translations.literal: In Tianfu, Jin's ancestor was at Ye; An Chongrong rebelled at Zhen Prefecture, leading several tens of thousands toward the capital. Jin's ancestor ordered Du Chongwei to command the generals to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianfu, while the Jin founder was at Ye, An Chongrong rebelled at Zhenzhou and marched tens of thousands toward the capital. The founder ordered Du Chongwei to lead the generals against him.

sentences.zh: 時延遇不預其行，乃泣告晉祖，願以身先，許之。

translations.literal: At the time Yanyu was not included in the expedition; he wept and told Jin's ancestor he wished to take the lead in person, and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyu had not been assigned to the campaign; he wept before the founder and begged to lead the charge, and was granted leave.

sentences.zh: 及陣於宗城，延遇率其屬先犯之，斬級數十，戰既酣，而劍亦折，諸將由是推伏。

translations.literal: When they formed battle lines at Zongcheng, Yanyu led his followers to strike first, beheading several tens of heads. When the battle grew fierce his sword also broke; the generals thereby submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Zongcheng he led his men in the first assault and took dozens of heads; when the fighting grew fierce his sword snapped, and the other generals were won to admiration.

sentences.zh: 晉祖聞之，即命中使以寶劍良馬賜之。

translations.literal: Jin's ancestor heard this and immediately ordered a palace envoy to gift him a treasured sword and fine horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder heard of this and at once sent a palace envoy with a treasured sword and fine horse as reward.

sentences.zh: 常山平，以功授檢校司徒，充馬軍左廂都校。

translations.literal: When Changshan was pacified, for merit he was appointed Acting Situ and made commander of the cavalry left wing.
translations.idiomatic: After Changshan was pacified he was made Acting Minister of Education and commander of the left wing of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後出為汾州刺史，遷復州防禦使。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Fen Prefecture prefect, then was moved to Fu Prefecture defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as prefect of Fenzhou, then as defense commissioner of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 國初，加檢校太保，尋受代歸闕。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was added Acting Grand Guardian; soon he was relieved and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he was made Acting Grand Guardian; soon he was relieved and recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 屬太祖親征兗海，以延遇為先鋒都校，兗州平，授齊州防禦使。

translations.literal: When Taizu personally campaigned in Yanhai, Yanyu was made vanguard commander; when Yan Prefecture was pacified he was appointed Qi Prefecture defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu campaigned in person against Yanhai, Yanyu was named vanguard commander; after Yanzhou fell he was made defense commissioner of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，改兗州防禦使。

translations.literal: After a year and more he was changed to Yan Prefecture defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Yanzhou as defense commissioner.

sentences.zh: 在兗二年，為政有聞，人甚安之，州民數百詣闕，乞立德政碑以頌其美。

translations.literal: In Yan for two years his governance was renowned; people were greatly at ease. Several hundred prefectural residents went to court begging to erect a monument of virtuous government to praise his excellence.
translations.idiomatic: During two years at Yanzhou his rule won wide praise and the people lived in peace; several hundred residents petitioned the throne to erect a monument celebrating his virtuous administration.

sentences.zh: 顯德二年冬，世宗命宰臣李穀為淮南道軍都部署，乃詔延遇為先鋒都校。

translations.literal: In winter of Xiande's second year, Shizong appointed chief minister Li Gu as overall deployer of the Huainan circuit army, and then ordered Yanyu as vanguard commander.
translations.idiomatic: That winter in the second year of Xiande, Shizong named Chief Minister Li Gu overall deployer of the Huainan army and appointed Yanyu vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 三年春，帥其所部與韓令坤先入揚州，軍聲甚振，尋命以別部屯於盛唐，前後敗淮賊萬餘眾。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year he led his troops with Han Lingkun to enter Yangzhou first; military renown was greatly stirred. Soon he was ordered with a separate division to encamp at Shengtang; before and after he defeated more than ten thousand Huai rebels.
translations.idiomatic: That spring he and Han Lingkun led their troops into Yangzhou ahead of the main force, and the army's prestige soared. He was then ordered to encamp a separate division at Shengtang and in repeated engagements routed more than ten thousand Huai rebels.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，世宗回自壽春，制以延遇為同州節度使，未赴任，復命帥眾南征。

translations.literal: In summer of the fourth year Shizong returned from Shouchun; by decree Yanyu was made Tong Prefecture military governor. Before he could take up the post he was again ordered to lead troops south in campaign.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Shizong returned from Shouchun and appointed Yanyu military governor of Tongzhou, but before he could take up the post he was ordered south again at the head of an army.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，以疾卒於濠州城下。

translations.literal: That winter he died of illness below the walls of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness that winter beneath the walls of Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太尉。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously gifted Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The throne posthumously honored him as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 唐景思，秦州人也。

translations.literal: Tang Jinsi was a man of Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jinsi came from Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼以屠狗為業，善角觝戲。

translations.literal: In youth he took dog-butcher as his trade and was skilled at grappling contests.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he worked as a dog butcher and excelled at wrestling.

sentences.zh: 初事偽蜀為軍校。

translations.literal: He first served false Shu as an army officer.
translations.idiomatic: He first served the puppet Shu state as an army officer.

sentences.zh: 唐同光中，莊宗命魏王繼岌帥師伐蜀，時景思以所部戍於固鎮，首以其城降於繼岌，乃授興州刺史，為貝州行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In Tang Tongguang, Zhuangzong ordered Prince of Wei Jiji to command troops against Shu. At the time Jinsi with his division garrisoned Guzhen and was first to surrender that city to Jiji; he was then appointed Xing Prefecture prefect and made Be Prefecture campaign marshal.
translations.idiomatic: During Tongguang, Zhuangzong sent Prince Jiji of Wei against Shu. Jinsi was then garrisoning Guzhen and was the first to surrender the town to Jiji; he was made prefect of Xingzhou and campaign marshal of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 屬契丹攻其城，因陷於幕庭，趙延壽素知其名，令隸於帳下，署為所部壕寨使。

translations.literal: When the Khitans attacked his city he thereby fell into the tent court. Zhao Yanshou had long known his name and ordered him attached under his banner, appointing him as his division's trench-camp commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans attacked his city he fell into their camp. Zhao Yanshou, who had long known his reputation, took him into his service and appointed him trench-camp commissioner of his command.

sentences.zh: 開運末，契丹據中原，以景思為亳州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyun the Khitans held the Central Plains and made Jinsi Bozhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaiyun, when the Khitans held the Central Plains, Jinsi was made defense commissioner of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 領事之日，會草寇數萬攻圍其城，景思悉力以拒之。

translations.literal: On the day he took office, it happened that several tens of thousands of grass-bandits attacked and besieged his city; Jinsi exerted all strength to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he took office, tens of thousands of bandits besieged the city, and Jinsi resisted with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 後數日城陷，景思挺身而出，使人告於鄰郡，得援軍數百，逐其草寇，復有其城，亳民賴是以濟。

translations.literal: Several days later the city fell. Jinsi stepped forth in person, sent men to report to neighboring prefectures, obtained several hundred relief troops, drove off the grass-bandits, and recovered his city; the people of Bo relied on this to be saved.
translations.idiomatic: Days later the city fell, but Jinsi sallied forth in person, sent word to neighboring prefectures, gathered several hundred relief troops, drove off the bandits, and recovered the city—the people of Bozhou were saved by his effort.

sentences.zh: 漢初，改授鄧州行軍司馬，常郁郁不得志，後受代歸闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he was changed and appointed Deng Prefecture campaign marshal; he was often depressed and without fulfillment of ambition; later he was relieved and returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Han he was reassigned as campaign marshal of Dengzhou, but remained discontented; later he was relieved and recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，命景思為沿淮巡檢使，屢挫淮賊。

translations.literal: In Qianyou he was ordered as inspector along the Huai, and repeatedly defeated Huai bandits.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou he was named inspector along the Huai and repeatedly defeated Huai rebels.

sentences.zh: 時史宏肇淫刑黷貨，多織羅南北富商殺之，奪其財，大開告密之門。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Hongzhao used excessive punishments and greedy goods; he often wove nets around north-south wealthy merchants, killed them, and seized their wealth, greatly opening the door to secret denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shi Hongzhao abused the law for profit, entrapping wealthy merchants from north and south, executing them and seizing their goods, while encouraging a flood of secret denunciations.

sentences.zh: 景思部下有仆夫，希求無厭，雖委曲待之，不滿其心，一日拂衣而去，見宏肇，言景思受淮南厚賂，私貯器械，欲為內應。

translations.literal: Under Jinsi was a servant who desired without end; though Jinsi treated him with forbearance, his heart was not satisfied. One day he shook out his robes and left, saw Hongzhao, and said Jinsi received thick bribes from Huainan, privately stored weapons, and wished to be an inner collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: A servant in Jinsi's household was insatiably greedy; though Jinsi treated him generously, the man was never satisfied. One day he stormed off to Hongzhao and accused Jinsi of taking heavy bribes from Huainan, hoarding weapons, and plotting to act as an enemy within.

sentences.zh: 宏肇即令親吏殿三十騎往收之，告者謂收吏曰：「景思多力，十夫之敵也，見便殺之，不然則無及矣。

translations.literal: Hongzhao immediately ordered his close officials to lead thirty horsemen to seize him. The accuser told the arresting officers: 'Jinsi has great strength—the match of ten men. If you see him, kill him at once; otherwise it will be too late.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao at once sent thirty horsemen under a trusted officer to seize him. The accuser told the arresting party: 'Jinsi is immensely strong—the equal of ten men. Kill him on sight, or you will never take him alive.

sentences.zh: 」收騎至，景思迎接。

translations.literal: ' The arresting horsemen arrived; Jinsi went out to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: ' When the horsemen arrived, Jinsi came out to meet them.

sentences.zh: 有欲擒之者，景思以兩手抱之，大呼曰：「冤哉！

translations.literal: When some wished to seize him, Jinsi with both hands embraced one of them and cried loudly: 'Injustice!
translations.idiomatic: As some moved to seize him, Jinsi seized one man in both arms and cried out: 'This is injustice!

sentences.zh: 景思何罪？

translations.literal: What crime has Jinsi?
translations.idiomatic: What crime have I committed?

sentences.zh: 設若有罪，死亦非晚，何不容披雪？

translations.literal: If indeed there is crime, death is also not early—why not allow clearing of snow?
translations.idiomatic: If I am guilty, death can wait—why not let the truth be heard?

sentences.zh: 公等皆丈夫，安忍如此！

translations.literal: You gentlemen are all men—how can you bear this!
translations.idiomatic: You are all men of honor—how can you bear to do this!

sentences.zh: 」都將命釋之，引告者面證景思，言受淮南賂。

translations.literal: ' The commander ordered him released, brought the accuser to confront Jinsi face to face, who spoke of receiving Huainan bribes.
translations.idiomatic: ' The commander ordered him released and brought the accuser face to face with Jinsi, who repeated the charge of Huainan bribes.

sentences.zh: 景思曰：「我從人家人並在此，若有十緡貯積，亦是受賂。

translations.literal: Jinsi said: 'My followers and family are all here. If there is stored wealth of even ten strings of cash, that too is receiving bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi said: 'My servants and household are all here. Search them—if you find so much as ten strings of cash laid by, count it as proof of bribery.

sentences.zh: 言我貯甲仗，除官賜外，有一事亦是私貯。

translations.literal: They say I stored armor and weapons; apart from official grants, there is one matter that is also private storage.
translations.idiomatic: You say I hoarded arms and armor—aside from what the court bestowed, there is one thing I did keep privately.

sentences.zh: 」使者搜索其家，惟衣一笥，軍籍糧簿而已，乃寬之。

translations.literal: ' The envoys searched his house and found only one chest of clothes, military registers, and grain accounts—thereupon they relaxed the case against him.
translations.idiomatic: ' The envoys searched his home and found only a single chest of clothing, military rolls, and grain ledgers, and so eased their suspicion.

sentences.zh: 景思曰：「使但械系送我入京。

translations.literal: Jinsi said: 'Envoy, simply shackle me and escort me to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi said: 'Sir, put me in chains and take me to the capital.

sentences.zh: 」先是，景思別有紀綱王知權者，在京，聞景思被誣，乃見史宏肇曰：「唐景思赤心為國，某服事三十年，孝於父母，義於朋友，被此誣罔，何以伸陳。

translations.literal: ' Earlier, Jinsi had another steward named Wang Zhiquan in the capital. Hearing Jinsi was slandered, he went to see Shi Hongzhao and said: 'Tang Jinsi is red-hearted in serving the state. I have served him thirty years—filial to parents, righteous to friends—and he suffers this false accusation; how can it be set forth?
translations.idiomatic: ' Earlier, Jinsi had a steward named Wang Zhiquan in the capital. When he heard Jinsi had been slandered, he went to Shi Hongzhao and said: 'Tang Jinsi has served the state with a loyal heart. I have served him thirty years; he is filial to his parents and faithful to his friends. How can such a false charge stand?

sentences.zh: 某請先下獄，願公追劾景思，免至冤橫。

translations.literal: I beg to enter prison first, wishing that Your Excellency pursue and examine Jinsi, sparing him from wrongful ruin.
translations.idiomatic: I ask to be imprisoned first, and beg Your Excellency to investigate Jinsi thoroughly, that he may not suffer unjust destruction.

sentences.zh: 」宏肇湣之，令在獄，日與酒食。

translations.literal: ' Hongzhao pitied him and ordered him held in prison, daily provided with wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: ' Hongzhao took pity on him and had him held in prison, with wine and food brought each day.

sentences.zh: 景思既桎梏就路，潁、亳之人隨至京師，眾保證之。

translations.literal: When Jinsi was already in fetters on the road, people of Ying and Bo followed to the capital, and the multitude vouched for him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jinsi was shackled and on the road to the capital, people from Yingzhou and Bozhou followed all the way to the capital, and crowds came forward to attest to his innocence.

sentences.zh: 宏肇乃令鞫告事者，具伏誣陷，即斬之，遂奏釋景思。

translations.literal: Hongzhao then ordered the accuser interrogated; he fully confessed to false framing and was immediately beheaded. Thereupon he memorialized to release Jinsi.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao then had the accuser interrogated; he confessed fully to the false charge and was beheaded at once. Hongzhao then memorialized for Jinsi's release.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，河東劉崇帥眾來寇，世宗親總六師以禦之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, Hedong's Liu Chong led troops to raid; Shizong personally commanded the six armies to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiande, Liu Chong of Hedong led an army in invasion, and Shizong took personal command of the imperial forces to meet him.

sentences.zh: 及陣於高平，景思於世宗馬前距踴數四，且曰：「願賜臣堅甲一聯，以觀臣之效用。

translations.literal: When they formed battle lines at Gaoping, Jinsi before Shizong's horse leaped and stamped several times, saying: 'I beg to be granted one suit of stout armor, to show your servant's usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: At the battle lines at Gaoping, Jinsi leaped and stamped four times before Shizong's horse and said: 'Grant me a suit of stout armor, that Your Majesty may see what I can do.

sentences.zh: 」世宗由是知其名，因以高平陣所得降軍數千人，署為效順指揮，命景思董之，使於淮上。

translations.literal: ' Shizong thereby came to know his name. He therefore took several thousand surrendered troops gained at the Gaoping formation, appointed them as the Xiaoshun command, ordered Jinsi to supervise them, and sent him to the Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: ' Shizong thus learned his name. He took several thousand enemy soldiers captured at Gaoping, organized them as the Loyal Submission command, placed Jinsi in charge, and sent him to the Huai frontier.

sentences.zh: 三年春，世宗親征淮甸，景思繼有戰功，乃命遙領饒州刺史。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year Shizong personally campaigned in the Huai region; Jinsi continued to have battle merit, and was then ordered to remotely hold Raozhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: That spring in the third year, when Shizong campaigned in person in the Huai region, Jinsi won repeated victories and was named prefect of Raozhou in absentia.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改授濠州行刺史，令帥眾攻圍濠州。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed and appointed acting prefect of Hao Prefecture, ordered to lead troops to attack and besiege Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting prefect of Haozhou and ordered to lead troops in the siege of that city.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，因力戰，為賊鋒所傷，數日而卒。

translations.literal: In winter of the fourth year, because of fierce fighting he was wounded by the rebel vanguard and died within several days.
translations.idiomatic: That winter in the fourth year he was wounded in fierce fighting by the enemy vanguard and died within days.

sentences.zh: 世宗甚憫之，詔贈武清軍節度使。

translations.literal: Shizong greatly pitied him; an edict posthumously gifted him military governor of the Wuqing army.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong mourned him deeply and posthumously honored him as military governor of the Wuqing army.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：自古為人臣者，望重則必危，功崇則難保，自非賢者，疇能免之。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: From antiquity, those who serve as ministers—when their prestige is heavy they must be endangered, when their merit is lofty they are hard to preserve. Unless they are worthy men, who can escape this?
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: From antiquity, ministers whose prestige grew heavy were always imperiled, and those whose merit towered high were hard to preserve—only the truly worthy could escape such a fate.

sentences.zh: 況王鄴帥昧明哲之規，周太祖乃雄猜之主，欲無及禍，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, Wang as Ye commander lacked enlightened and wise rules, while Zhou's Taizu was a heroic and suspicious ruler—wishing to avoid reaching calamity, how could it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yin, lord of Ye, lacked the foresight of a sage, and Taizu of Zhou was a ruler both formidable and suspicious—how could he hope to escape disaster?

sentences.zh: 自福進而下，皆將帥之英也，擁旌作翰，諒亦宜然。

translations.literal: From Fujin downward, all were heroes among generals and commanders; bearing banners as pillars of state, it may be believed this was also fitting.
translations.idiomatic: From He Fujin onward, each was a paragon among commanders; to bear imperial banners as pillars of the realm was only what their merit deserved.

sentences.zh: 惟彥超以捍寇而沒，可不謂忠乎！

translations.literal: Only Yanchao perished in resisting bandits—can this not be called loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: Only Yanchao fell while holding the enemy at bay—surely that may be called loyalty!
